title: The Number You're Given
logline: A public office fills up on a busy morning, everyone holding a number and a folder, and the queue moves slowly enough that the room's mood becomes the only thing happening.
human_question: What does an ordinary wait, with nothing at stake but time, still manage to stir up in us?

situation.what_happens: A room where nothing can be hurried collects people who all need one small thing signed, stamped or confirmed, and hands each of them a number instead of an answer. The wait is not dramatic and nobody is being wronged; the counter is working as fast as it can. What fills the morning is the small arithmetic of place-keeping, papers checked and re-checked, and the discovery halfway through that a document is missing and the morning was wasted. In the same room, and just as often, somebody helps a stranger fill in a form.
situation.who_is_involved: People who have taken a day off work to be there; the clerks at the counter, who receive every person's whole morning as a request and can only answer some of them; whoever is helping an older relative through the paperwork; and the people at home waiting to hear whether it went through.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A day of lost earnings for most people in the room, and for a few of them something that actually matters: a payment, a permission, a certificate without which something else cannot begin. For the clerks, being the visible face of a process they do not control. For the film, not mocking people waiting and not making officials into villains.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins full and thins slowly. The pressures are the clock, the discovery of missing papers, and the fact that nobody can tell how long anything will take. It ends with most people served, a few turned away to come back another day, and the room empty. Reality decides who is in it, and the mornings when nothing much happens are the normal ones.

concept_merge.why_together: C022 supplies the constant: restlessness is one of the four factors present in every unwholesome mind, a mind that will not settle on what is in front of it [C022-P:L31]. C007 supplies the occasion in its smallest form, a request refused or simply not yet granted [C007-P:L49; C007-M:L17], with both hate-rooted minds always carrying a painful mental feeling [C007-P:L25–L28]. Together they describe the group's question at the lowest temperature it reaches anywhere: life refusing what people want, where what they want is only to be seen next.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That nothing has to go wrong for this state to appear, and that the same room produces unprompted kindness at the same rate. Neither concept predicts the second half of that; only sitting in the room does.

concept_links.why: Restlessness is one of the four factors both sources place in every unwholesome mind, present whatever else is [C022-P:L31; C022-M:L3]. A slow queue is that unsettledness in its smallest, least dramatic daily form. The wind-in-the-leaves comparison this link previously used is not among the similes the digest records for this source, and has been removed rather than re-attributed.

The group's question in miniature: not getting what one wants is named among the occasions [C007-P:L49], and Margaya's list includes a request not granted [C007-M:L17]. Here the thing wanted is only to be called next. The four constant factors describe every unwholesome moment in anyone, so nothing in this material may be used to characterise either the public or the clerks as a kind of person.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The texts name a request not granted among the commonest occasions for displeasure, and they count a mind that will not settle as present in every harmful moment. A slow morning at a counter is the smallest possible version of both, and it shows that this heat needs no wrongdoing at all, only a wait.
what_must_be_real: The office, its staff and its visitors must be filmed as they genuinely are on an ordinary day, with permission from the office and consent from anyone shown closely. No delay, dispute or kindness may be arranged, and no member of the public may be filmed in a moment of real difficulty with their paperwork without their agreement afterwards.
position_hint: middle, if it were used: the group's quietest version of its own question, best placed where the heat is lowest. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Mocking members of the public shown frustrated or waiting.
Portraying officials unfairly as the source of the frustration.
Formal permission requirements for filming inside a public office, and the pressure those create on what can be shown.
Reading the four constant factors as a description of a type of person rather than of a moment.
drop_if: No office grants filming permission for a genuinely busy day.
Visitors are unwilling to be shown.

connections.note: Its counters, numbers and half-finished paperwork are folded into the household film, where the same waiting is what a long decision is actually made of.
Two waiting rooms, a roadside and a counter, testing the same small patience.

selection.reason: Sound but slight on its own, and duplicative of IDEA-0038's public wait; its counter-and-number strand is folded into IDEA-0045, where the waiting has a decision attached to it.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
